decisions.reason: The downward spout direction does not change the selected bowl capacity, depth, or form.
The decision changes spout geometry, while the candidate's valve, button interaction, gravity drive, and controlled-flow requirements remain unchanged.
Spout pour orientation does not alter whisk size, style, material, attachment, or operating depth.
The source changes pour direction but does not change sealing or leak-prevention requirements.
Custom fabrication of render-style spouts is already required; specifying their downward pour direction does not change the candidate's sourcing policy or V1 priority.
The product-level spout detail may be reflected in design work, but it does not change the system-layout deliverable, its required completion state, or its scope.
Downward pouring does not change the requirement that the spout be removable or readily cleanable.
The source concerns preserving drink consistency during dispensing, not changing the required mixing or frothing result.
The downward pour direction does not change the platform height, cup clearance, configuration, or mixer fit.
The source references the rendering only for spout direction and does not change branding text, placard placement, or display sides.
The source identifies a dispensing-consistency benefit but does not change splash-control behavior or mitigation measures during mixing.
Spout pour geometry does not affect bowl removal, swapping, cleaning access, or whisk and motor clearance.
